significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) ordering and predictive coupling: "the pretraining checkpoint at which a belief becomes linearly decodable predicts the checkpoint at which that belief becomes context-unrevisable," beyond frequency and difficulty. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon—acquisition followed by increasing resistance to contradictory context—and a form-(ii) mechanism in which a "strengthening parametric-recall component and declining context reliance" causally produces rigidity; together these constrain when future facts should become entrenched and explain why interventions on consolidation restore revision. This bears directly on the parametric-versus-contextual conflict documented in Xie et al.'s ICLR 2024 work, "Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth," while a negative result would still distinguish uncoupled timelines, immediate entrenchment, or absence of a shared consolidation mechanism rather than merely report a failed search. True and false are determinate states, and the topic-substitution check passes: replacing the checkpoint ordering and causal coupling with the generic LLM-belief topic would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The concrete handles are the per-fact "acquisition and entrenchment checkpoints," the predictive "context-vs-prior reliance" signal, and the proposed "checkpoint-aware RAG diagnostics" and "training-time revisability regularisers." The acquisition signal is ex ante because it forecasts later context-unrevisability during pretraining, leaving an action window for training or checkpoint selection, rather than only explaining a conflict after it occurs. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive acquisition-to-entrenchment ordering and coupling would predict what should be found, so this is a transferable relation rather than merely a procedure for rediscovering an arbitrary direction; however, the claim itself concedes that available evidence is limited to Pythia/OLMo-style regimes and "may not transfer to other pretraining regimes or to very large closed models." Downstream users could include model trainers and RAG auditors, and the topic-substitution check passes because those users receive a timing-based predictor and intervention target that the generic study of LLM beliefs does not supply.
